title: Choose Cortex's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Blue Book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Blue Book
options.lineage: university exam blue books, graded in the margin
options.thesis: Every answer is handed in like an exam and graded claim by claim in the margin.
options.viewport: Blue-book-blue left rail with the Cortex wordmark; a centred answer column with a thin vertical margin rule; verification ticks (blue ✓, graphite ~, red ✗) sit in that margin beside each claim; one quiet status line above the ask bar.
options.risk: Reads as a school costume if the ruled-paper or handwriting is taken literally; it must stay a clean app.

raised.raise: Every step in the status line carries its elapsed time, and Fast Mode shows its time budget, like sides that must not overflow the tape.
Evidence lists use a strict hairline grid with compact rows: no card-padding inflation.
The trace is set at one type size; rank is carried by weight, case and colour only.
Hovering a citation lifts its evidence and dims the rest.
Upcoming deadlines are time-ranked rows whose state (moved, at risk) restyles the row without breaking the grid.

options.label: Sidenote Paper
options.lineage: scholarly papers with numbered references and Tufte-style sidenotes
options.thesis: Answers read like a well-referenced paper: claims in the column, sources in the margin beside them.
options.viewport: A narrow reading column with a wide right margin; each citation appears as a sidenote aligned to its sentence; the ask bar is a single line at the foot.
options.risk: The most familiar 'editorial AI' look; risks broadsheet-hairline clichés and reads less like a product.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.lineage: metro line diagrams, translated to a light ground
options.thesis: Each source is a coloured line; the agent's plan is a route with sub-questions as stations.
options.viewport: Standard sidebar and answer column; the trace is a small route diagram whose lines light up as each source is searched.
options.case: Fuses well for the trace (plan as route, sources as lines) but its midnight ground fights the light-default brand, and students don't identify with it as strongly.
options.risk: Becomes a decorative map if the diagram grows past the status line.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: Side A / Side B tracklists timed to fit the tape.
options.case: Loses both axes: nostalgic for this audience and nothing in it says cited answers.
options.kept: Exact time budgeting: every step shows its running time.

options.label: High-density modules
options.thesis: Hundreds of ruled modules on one screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: you explicitly ruled out a dense dashboard.
options.kept: A strict hairline border system with no whitespace inflation.

options.label: Timetable slide rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: Raked slides along a lit bed.
options.case: Loses both axes: raked containers hurt reading and the world is foreign to students.
options.kept: Single-size type with rank carried by weight and case (used for the trace).

options.label: Streaming title wall
options.thesis: The focused tile grows; everything else dims.
options.case: Loses both axes: entertainment framing, poster art you don't have.
options.kept: Focus lifts one item and dims its neighbours (citation hover).

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: Time-ranked rows that restyle on delay.
options.case: Loses both axes: an instrument costume, and flap animation is noise.
options.kept: Rows ranked by time whose state restyles the row (Upcoming in Brief).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Perplexity/Linear-style neutral assistant, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Grey sidebar, centred chat column, rounded answer card, sources as a chip row.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every AI wrapper by design.
